---
title: "Digital Media Technologies and Creative Production for Games"
toc: false
format: lesson-html
---

This course studies the media that a game is made of beyond its code: story
and screenwriting, storyboards, sound, music and sound effects, video, and the
intellectual-property rules that govern digital content. Students learn to
analyse and evaluate these media in terms of the player's experience, and to
produce them with digital tools.

**Textbook.** Schell, J. *The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses*, 3rd ed.,
CRC Press, 2019. References: Collins, K. *Game Sound*, MIT Press, 2008;
McKee, R. *Story*, HarperCollins, 1997.

**How to study each lesson.** Read the lesson notes (PDF) before and after the
lecture. Use the interactive lesson page to practise: it has questions with
instant feedback and mini-games (the PDF links to them with QR codes). The
slides are a short summary for revision.

## Lectures

Lectures of 60 minutes (lecture and seminar), in teaching order, with a homework after every two lectures. Faded lectures are not available yet.
